subject: general
question: Where is the Genome India data officially hosted during its launch in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Biological Data Centre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Genome India Project was initiated to map the entire genome of the Indian population to create a comprehensive database to aid in personalized medicine, disease prevention, and healthcare research.
 
• During its launch in 2025, the official repository for the Genome India data was the **Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC)**, located in Faridabad, Haryana.
 
• The Indian Biological Data Centre was established by the Department of Biotechnology (DBT), Government of India, and is the first national repository for life science data in the country.
 
• The IBDC adheres to the principles of data sharing and open access, promoting accessibility for the scientific community while ensuring data security and privacy.
 
• The Genome India Project is a collaborative effort involving 20 academic and research institutions across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Genome India Project:**

 
 
• The project aims to collect, decode, and analyze the genetic information of 10,000 Indian individuals, representing the country’s diverse population.
 
• The initiative is expected to play a critical role in advancing precision medicine and understanding genetic factors behind diseases.
 
• This project aligns with global initiatives like the Human Genome Project and the UK Biobank project.
 
 
 
• **Indian Biological Data Centre (IBDC):**
 
 
• The IBDC is a state-of-the-art data storage and analysis facility, housing biological data generated from Indian research labs and institutions.
 
• The center supports various domains, including genomics, proteomics, and biomedical data analysis.
 
• It ensures compliance with international data sharing standards while safeguarding data privacy.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Genomic Data:**
 
 
• Genomic data can be utilized for early disease detection, personalized treatment plans, and drug development.
 
• It also helps in understanding genetic predispositions to diseases and identifying potential therapeutic targets.
 
• The data is critical for research in agricultural and environmental science as well.
 
 
 
• **Precision Medicine:**
 
 
• Precision medicine tailors treatment plans based on an individual’s genetic makeup, lifestyle, and environment.
 
• It is particularly effective for complex diseases such as cancer, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases.
 
• The Genome India Project is expected to advance precision medicine in India.
